paper_title: Training and Evaluating with Human Label Variation An Empirical Study
caption: Soft accuracy and graphs for a binary classification problem on a single example where the true and the predicted judgement for the positive class is 0.5 and q respectively.

annotations.annotation: The plot illustrates the relationship between a parameter q and two measures, "soft accuracy" and "PO-JSD." The x-axis is labeled q and uses a linear scale ranging from 0.0 to 1.0, with tick marks at intervals of 0.2. The y-axis, which represents both the "soft accuracy" and "PO-JSD," is also on a linear scale, spanning from 0.6 to 1.0 with similar tick intervals of 0.1. The blue line with no markers and a solid style represents "soft accuracy," starting at a value of 0.55 when q is 0.05, increasing linearly to a peak of 1.0 at q = 0.5, and then decreasing symmetrically back to 0.55 at q = 0.95. The orange line also has no markers and a solid style, representing the "PO-JSD," which starts just below 0.8 at q = 0.05, increases in a concave manner to reach a maximum of approximately 1.0 at q = 0.5, and then symmetrically decreases back to around 0.55 at q = 0.95. A legend is placed at the bottom-center of the plot describing the color pattern with corresponding measures.
